State-specific data quality issues for 2024
        The state-specific data quality issues noted below are of particular concern due to documented
evidence of underreporting and/or inaccurate reporting for 2024. These data should be used with
caution.

Father’s information: Changes in delivery room/hospital policy in response to the COVID-19 pandemic
(2020-2023), may have influenced a general increase in unknown information for fathers and an
increase in a “No” response for paternity acknowledgements.

notes.text: RF_PPTERM records a history of previous preterm birth. It is not the gestational age or preterm status of the current delivery. All eleven layouts retain Y=Yes, N=No, U=Unknown or not stated, with F_RF_PPB at position 324 (0=Non-Reporting, 1=Reporting). Preserve unknown and nonreporting states separately. Stable codes do not establish stable ascertainment.

The 2014–2017 quality sections explicitly flag previous preterm birth in New Mexico, and pregnancy risk factors in Virginia except eclampsia and previous cesarean delivery, for underreporting, inaccurate reporting or high unknowns. These concerns affect interpretation despite unchanged Y/N/U codes. The same warning is not listed in the inspected 2018–2024 state-specific sections; omission alone is not proof that ascertainment became comparable.

For earlier years, preserve item-specific reporting flags and the distinction between revised-only and combined fields; identical code lists do not make the reporting populations identical.

The 2020–2024 quality sections warn that pandemic-related delivery-room or hospital policies may have increased unknown paternal information and No responses to paternity acknowledgment during 2020–2023. This is a potential ascertainment change rather than a change in the numeric source codes.

NCHS switched its principal gestational-age measure to the obstetric estimate in 2014; a trend using earlier LMP-based published preterm rates is not a continuous measure. The candidate current-delivery preterm rule uses OEGest_Comb 17–36 weeks among known 17–47 weeks; code 99 is unknown. This is distinct from RF_PPTERM.

notes.text: Field length tells a fixed-width parser how many character positions to read. The 2014–2022 guides print MRACE6 at position 107 with length 2, although the next field starts at 108; following both instructions literally would overlap the adjacent field and could corrupt extraction. The 2023–2024 guides print length 1. Codes 1–6 and their meanings are unchanged in these layout blocks, so this is a layout-documentation issue rather than evidence of a race-category change. Preserve the printed discrepancy and validate parsing against record positions and observed code domains.

The complete 2015 U.S. source contains 2,923 occurrence records with MRACE31=99, MRACE6=9 and MRACE15=99 together. These codes are absent from the corresponding annual layout entries. Their meanings are not established here; they are preserved literally without race-category labels or automatic missing-value conversion. All other nonblank MRACE6/MRACE15 pairs follow the documented aggregation. This is a source-data observation, not a harmonization decision.

notes.text: The 2014–2015 RF_INFTR description points to reporting flag position 319, but position 319 is the pre-pregnancy diabetes reporting flag. Position 328 is filler in those guides; F_RF_INFT appears there in 2016–2024. The existing conversion nevertheless includes F_RF_INFT in 2014 and omits it in 2015–2017. These mismatches require source/import-specification review; no earlier flag is silently substituted.

The 2024 guide flags infertility treatment, fertility-enhancing drugs and assisted reproductive technology for Georgia and North Carolina as not reported because system errors affected accuracy. Use the appropriate annual reporting flags; a blank/nonreporting value is not a negative response.

notes.text: RF_PPTERM records a history of previous preterm birth. It is not the gestational age or preterm status of the current delivery. All eleven layouts retain Y=Yes, N=No, U=Unknown or not stated, with F_RF_PPB at position 324 (0=Non-Reporting, 1=Reporting). Preserve unknown and nonreporting states separately. Stable codes do not establish stable ascertainment.

The 2014–2017 quality sections explicitly flag previous preterm birth in New Mexico, and pregnancy risk factors in Virginia except eclampsia and previous cesarean delivery, for underreporting, inaccurate reporting or high unknowns. These concerns affect interpretation despite unchanged Y/N/U codes. The same warning is not listed in the inspected 2018–2024 state-specific sections; omission alone is not proof that ascertainment became comparable.
